questions.q: What happened just as Mr. Fogg was leaving the Calcutta station?
choices: Fix walked up and asked to share a carriage to the docks
A policeman asked him and his servant to follow him
The captain of the Rangoon came to meet him
Aouda's relative arrived to take her home
questions.evidence: Be so good, both of you, as to follow me.

questions.q: Why did Mr. Fogg obey the policeman without any fuss?
choices: He was afraid of being beaten with the stick
He thought the policeman was a friend of Fix
To an Englishman, the law is sacred
He wanted to see the city before the ship left
questions.evidence: law is sacred to an Englishman

questions.q: What did Aouda say to Mr. Fogg once they were locked in the room?
choices: That he must leave her, since he was in trouble for saving her
That her relative in Calcutta would surely pay for a good lawyer to help
That she would tell the judge what the priests had done
That she wanted to go back to Bombay by herself
questions.evidence: Sir, you must leave me to my fate!

questions.q: "We shall be on board by noon," replied his master, placidly. What does "placidly" mean here?
choices: Angrily and loudly
Calmly, without worry
Sadly, almost in tears
Quickly, in a rush

questions.q: What funny mix-up happened when Judge Obadiah came into court?
choices: He sat in the clerk's chair by mistake
He put on his clerk's wig instead of his own
He called out the wrong prisoner's name first of all
He forgot his glasses and could not read

questions.q: Why did Passepartout watch the big clock over the judge so nervously?
choices: He was hungry and wanted lunch at noon
The steamer for Hong Kong was leaving at noon
Fix had told him the trial would last all day
He had promised to meet Aouda's cousin at ten
questions.evidence: But the steamer leaves at noon!

questions.q: Who came into the court-room as the complainants?
choices: Three Indian priests
Sir Francis Cromarty and the guide
The rajah's guards from Pillaji
Fix and the British consul

questions.q: Fogg and Passepartout first thought the charge was about the rescue at Pillaji. What was it really about?
choices: Buying an elephant without a proper permit
Passepartout entering the pagoda on Malabar Hill in Bombay
Riding on a railway line that was not finished
Leaving their Bombay hotel without paying the bill for their rooms
questions.evidence: but of the pagoda of Malabar Hill, at Bombay

questions.q: What proof did the clerk put on his desk?
choices: Passepartout's lost straw hat
A pair of shoes left behind
A torn piece of his coat
His ticket from the train
questions.evidence: here are the desecrator's very shoes

questions.q: Why was Passepartout's cry of "My shoes!" a mistake?
choices: It made the crowd laugh and angered the judge
It admitted that he was the one who had entered the pagoda
It woke Aouda, who had fallen asleep on the bench
It told Fix exactly where the carpet-bag full of banknotes was kept
questions.evidence: permitting this imprudent exclamation to escape him

questions.q: How had Fix set up the arrest in Calcutta?
choices: He promised the Bombay priests money and sent them to Calcutta
He wrote to the judge pretending to be one of the priests from Pillaji
He paid the policeman to invent a charge against Fogg
He followed Fogg on the elephant and told the guards
questions.evidence: he promised them a goodly sum in damages

questions.q: What sentence did the judge give Passepartout?
choices: A week in prison and a fine of 150 pounds
Fifteen days in prison and a fine of 300 pounds
Thirty days in prison and no fine at all
A fine of 1,000 pounds but no prison
questions.evidence: imprisonment for fifteen days and a fine of three hundred pounds

questions.q: Why was Fix pleased when Fogg was sentenced to a week in prison?
choices: The warrant would have time to arrive while Fogg was held
He would get to keep the fines that Fogg paid
He could take the next ship to Hong Kong ahead of Fogg
He would finally be able to search Fogg's carpet-bag
questions.evidence: it would be more than time for the warrant to arrive

questions.q: How did Fogg avoid going to prison?
choices: He proved to the judge that the shoes belonged to someone else
He offered bail and paid 1,000 pounds for each of them
He asked the British consul to set them free
He escaped through the barred window of the room

questions.q: What was Passepartout's joke about his shoes when they were handed back?
choices: They were worth more than a thousand pounds apiece and pinched his feet
They were the only things he had managed to keep from all of India so far
They would bring him luck for the rest of the voyage
They were far too big and he would give them to Fix
questions.evidence: More than a thousand pounds apiece; besides, they pinch my feet.

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Fogg being tried in Calcutta for Passepartout's act in Bombay, and paying bail to leave
Passepartout rescuing Aouda for a second time from the priests of Pillaji
Fix finally arresting Fogg after the warrant arrives from London
Aouda telling the judge the story of her life in Bombay
questions.evidence: Meanwhile, you are liberated on bail.
